Question: At the grocery store last week, small boxes of facial tissue were priced at \(4\) boxes for \(\$5.\) This week they are on sale at \(5\) boxes for \(\$4.\) The percent decrease in the price per box during the sale was closest to
Solution:
Method 1: Compare prices per box

First put both offers on a per-box basis. Last week's price per box was \(5\div4=1.25\) dollars, while the sale price is \(4\div5=0.80\) dollars.

The decrease is \(1.25-0.80=0.45\) dollars per box. A percent decrease compares this drop with the original price, so it is
\[
\frac{0.45}{1.25}\times100\%=36\%.
\]
The choice \(35\%\) is one percentage point away, while every other choice is at least four percentage points away. The answer is \(35\%\), choice B.

Method 2: Compare the cost of 20 boxes

Compare the cost of \(20\) boxes, since that quantity can be bought in whole groups under either offer. Last week, \(20\) boxes formed five groups of four, costing \(5\cdot5=25\) dollars. This week, they form four groups of five, costing \(4\cdot4=16\) dollars.

For the same number of boxes, the cost drops by \(25-16=9\) dollars. Its percent decrease is
\[
\frac9{25}=\frac{36}{100}=36\%.
\]
This is also the percent decrease per box: multiplying both the original per-box price and its decrease by \(20\) leaves their ratio unchanged.

The closest listed value is \(35\%\), one percentage point away; all other choices are at least four percentage points away. The answer is choice B.
